clusters.label: AI, history & geopolitics
clusters.reason: Long conversations connecting models of intelligence with history and state power.

episodes.title: #392 – Joscha Bach: Life, Intelligence, Consciousness, AI & the Future of Humans
episodes.why: Explores cognitive architecture, artificial consciousness and open-source AI; speculative positions remain the guest's views.

books.title: Principles of Synthetic Intelligence: Psi: An Architecture of Motivated Cognition
books.author: Joscha Bach
books.why: Technical bridge from the conversation about minds to a specified cognitive architecture.

episodes.title: #289 – Stephen Kotkin: Putin, Zelenskyy, and War in Ukraine
episodes.why: Connects Russian and Soviet history with the 2022 invasion; analysis is dated to the recording rather than a current forecast.

books.title: Stalin: Paradoxes of Power, 1878–1928
books.author: Stephen Kotkin
books.why: Historical context for the discussion of Russian state power; this volume ends in 1928.

clusters.label: Money markets & financial systems
clusters.reason: Understand market plumbing and compare competing monetary-system explanations.

episodes.title: Zoltan Pozsar and Perry Mehrling On The Historic Crisis Of Financial Market Plumbing
episodes.why: A crisis-era explanation of funding stress and Federal Reserve intervention, useful before tackling rate transmission.

books.title: The New Lombard Street: How the Fed Became the Dealer of Last Resort
books.author: Perry Mehrling
books.why: Develops the money-market and central-bank framework behind the episode.

episodes.title: Zoltan Pozsar and Perry Mehrling Debate Bretton Woods 3.0
episodes.why: Contrasting interpretations of dollar dominance, commodities and monetary change; the thesis is debated rather than established.

books.title: The New Lombard Street: How the Fed Became the Dealer of Last Resort
books.author: Perry Mehrling
books.why: Develops the money-market and central-bank framework behind the episode.

clusters.label: Sleep & health optimisation
clusters.reason: Discovery seeds include Andrew Huberman, Matthew Walker and Bryan Johnson (the dictated Brian/Optimize interest); inclusion is not endorsement.

episodes.title: GUEST SERIES | Dr. Matt Walker: The Biology of Sleep & Your Unique Sleep Needs
episodes.why: Introduces sleep stages, chronotype and individual needs. Discussion and linked studies require claim-by-claim appraisal; this is not proven personalised advice.

books.title: Why We Sleep: Unlocking the Power of Sleep and Dreams
books.author: Matthew Walker
books.why: Longer treatment of sleep and circadian topics; publisher description verifies the book, not clinical claims.

episodes.title: The $2M Longevity Protocol: Bryan Johnson’s Biohacking Blueprint
episodes.why: Personal self-experiment and longevity ambitions described by Johnson. The official description is promotional; reversal-of-aging claims are not independently supported by this catalog. The sleep book is a separate topic bridge, not validation of Blueprint.

books.title: Why We Sleep: Unlocking the Power of Sleep and Dreams
books.author: Matthew Walker
books.why: Longer treatment of sleep and circadian topics; publisher description verifies the book, not clinical claims.

clusters.label: Urban orchards, soil & fungi
clusters.reason: Pair community-orchard observation with measured soil testing and a focused mycorrhizae book.

episodes.title: How to Read a Soil Test for Fruit Trees (and What to Try Next) with Ariel Agenbroad
episodes.why: An extension educator discusses pH, organic matter and test interpretation, encouraging context before amendments.

books.title: Teaming with Fungi: The Organic Grower's Guide to Mycorrhizae
books.author: Jeff Lowenfels
books.why: Topic bridge from orchard soil life to plant–fungus relationships; applicability depends on species and site.

episodes.title: Why do some fruit trees thrive while others struggle? with Derek Barbe and Chrisina Balint
episodes.why: Visits two Peterborough community orchards to compare tree growth and soil biology. Site observations generate questions; they do not establish causal benefits of a product or practice.

books.title: Teaming with Fungi: The Organic Grower's Guide to Mycorrhizae
books.author: Jeff Lowenfels
books.why: Topic bridge from orchard soil life to plant–fungus relationships; applicability depends on species and site.

clusters.label: Espionage & unusual history
clusters.reason: Narrative history spanning intelligence operations and wartime amphetamine use.

episodes.title: Inside the Iranian Embassy Siege with Ben Macintyre
episodes.why: Author interview on the 1980 siege, hostage negotiations and intelligence context, with a direct bridge to the source book.

books.title: The Siege: A Six-Day Hostage Crisis and the Daring Special-Forces Operation That Shocked the World
books.author: Ben Macintyre
books.why: The book discussed in the interview, expanding the 1980 embassy-crisis reconstruction.

episodes.title: #481 – Norman Ohler: Hitler, Nazis, Drugs, WW2, Blitzkrieg, LSD, MKUltra & CIA
episodes.why: Includes Pervitin, military stimulant use and the author's response to historians' criticism. Drug use does not by itself establish an explanation for military outcomes.

books.title: Blitzed: Drugs in the Third Reich
books.author: Norman Ohler
books.why: Book behind the wartime-stimulant discussion; compare its interpretation with the criticism discussed in the episode.
